title: Prompt Result Readback V1 (what GET /api/projects/<id>/prompt-results answers)
$comment: Emitter: src/design_lab/prompt_results.py (PromptResults.readback). This envelope is the answer to the audit finding that the prompt routes produced a document and kept nothing: every result this service stored is listed with the sources it was assembled from, and every human signature about it is kept next to the digest it quoted. `state` distinguishes NONE (no result was ever produced here) from UNREVIEWED (produced, nobody signed) from NOT_CURRENT (signed, but the signature describes other bytes) -- collapsing those three is how an empty panel ends up reading as a rejected one. The prompt documents themselves are REFERENCED, not restated: `$defs/result.properties.document` points at prompt-composition-v1 and prompt-reversal-v1, and `review` points at prompt-result-review-v1, so one contract owns each shape and a change there moves in here by reference. `columns_match_document` is published rather than assumed: the scalar columns and the document must agree, and the store says which rows it checked.

total_readable.description: 可读出来的全部条数，分页前取的，不是这一页的条数。

results.description: 这一页。全部条数看 total_readable/result_count，是否还有下文看 truncated 与 next_offset；reviews 永远是全量，因为截断签收记录就是隐藏决定。

allOf.$comment: NONE is only ever the honest word for an empty store, and it may not coexist with a count. accepted_count is bounded by result_count for the same reason: a page cannot be allowed to print more signatures than there are documents.

The same rule read from the other side: a project with rows may never be reported as NONE, not even when every row is unreadable -- `unreadable_count` carries that case, and collapsing it into NONE would tell a reader this service never produced a prompt.
